text: I. Core Positioning of the DisciplineThe discipline of Artology focuses on the "existence and significance of art", exploring the origin (such as primitive rituals, labor practices), essence (such as emotional expression, aesthetic creation), form (such as visual art, auditory art, interdisciplinary art), creative laws (such as inspiration, technique, school styles), as well as the relationship between art and society, culture, and technology. It is not only a description of artistic phenomena, but also aims to reveal the unique value of art as a human spiritual activity - enriching people's spiritual world through aesthetic experiences and promoting cultural inheritance and innovation.II. Training ObjectivesTo cultivate comprehensive talents with a solid theoretical foundation in art, a broad humanistic perspective, and critical thinking, who can engage in professional work in fields such as art research, education, criticism, curating, and cultural management. Core competencies include: Master the basic theories such as art history, art theory, and aesthetics, and understand the characteristics and connections of different art forms;Have the ability to analyze art works (such as paintings, music, and films), and be able to interpret their forms, connotations, and the background of the times;Understand the cutting-edge developments in art (such as digital art, cross-media art), and possess the ability to apply theories to artistic practice or cultural dissemination.
